Measure m51 at 10/1 and 100 uL; predicted V1/V2 is 31.77/57.63 mL. The matched 50- and 150-uL observations 4fb92bd1fab3ba235858 and 19229d505f75d05a0bcb measured 37.67/57.93 and 26.24/55.67. This midpoint distinguishes onset curvature from linear interpolation while testing the much smaller completion response. It directly extends the latest substantial onset underestimate.

Measure secondary alcohol m60 at 10/1 and 150 uL; predicted 38.47/65.90 mL. The matched 100-uL record c352863d9fa4a8645481 measured 39.13/64.72. At 5/1, 985361f6699d97f9464f and 62d7ea74ab73fa6214b4 showed a substantial onset decrease between 50 and 100 uL. This tests whether that response continues at higher amount in weaker mobile phase, alongside the selected m51 midpoint.

Measure m60 at 2/1 and 50 uL; predicted 10.79/16.27 mL. Pair with the selected 150-uL point, holding density, PE loading solvent and its 300-uL volume fixed. The measured 5/1 pair 985361f6699d97f9464f and 62d7ea74ab73fa6214b4 differed by 7.98 mL in onset but only 2.22 mL in completion. The stronger-solvent pair tests whether the predicted attenuation of both loading responses is appropriate.

Measure the matched m60 2/1, 150-uL endpoint; predicted 10.76/16.28 mL. Its prediction is almost identical to the selected 50-uL point despite the threefold amount difference. Together these labels distinguish a condition-specific small loading response from the substantial onset response already measured at 5/1, supplying useful supervision whether attenuation is confirmed or contradicted.

Acquire another m92 5/1, 150-uL, 200-uL EA-loading catalog record; predicted 7.10/21.43 mL. The same recorded tuple in 6c1c34b12c66ebcf39a4 finished at 27.72 mL, whereas the latest 50- and 100-uL observations 790d27f0fa045d91f307 and d1eeb016c4cf20b87e92 finished at 21.06 and 19.96. Recurrence of the high-amount extension would support a completion upturn; a substantially earlier result would limit that interpretation. Low CW distance does not remove this hypothesis-discrimination value.

Measure m125 in neat EA at 150 uL sample with 300 uL DCM loading solvent; predicted 6.51/16.04 mL. The same protocol at 50 and 100 uL measured 4.87/12.85 and 5.28/11.22 in 55f2352b50967352163e and e7ed7ca4a53258b73ba2. This completes the 300-uL protocol's amount series and tests whether its completion remains earlier than the model's averaged prediction. Without a matched 500-uL protocol label at this amount, it cannot alone establish the protocol difference at 150 uL.

Measure bromopropionic acid m45 at 2/1 and 100 uL; predicted 5.98/5.86 mL. The predicted endpoint reversal and completion earlier than the measured neat-EA result fb031b748f1f5a8cc89e, 5.12/8.56, warrant a stronger-solvent anchor. The ordinary measured 5/1 and 20/1 records 5cc67d02b8fad1c648d6 and e6605c23fb1943a6b848 provide context. This tests the scope of an apparent response-shape failure without treating the negative completion in 129036e0bccc4ff7e848 as a physically interpretable interval.

Measure m73 at 2/1 and 50 uL; predicted 7.39/11.11 mL. Its 1/1 same-tuple records 7bd4e959319ef8b7b0fe and a387411cbcb6be48bde4 both had late onset but disagreed substantially, and the latter slightly reversed endpoint order. The nearby 2/1, 100-uL observation 49932dbd3d16bb64f71a measured 5.26/11.60. This low-amount boundary tests localization of late onset and prevents the unusual 1/1 labels from being extended across neighboring ratios.

Measure thiomethylacetophenone m128 at 2/1 and 50 uL; predicted 7.62/14.37 mL. At matched loading, cdcabd704ebeeeca9183 measured 21.00/34.02 at 5/1 and b655d7de0986cbd0d622 measured 7.57/15.82 at 1/1. This directly tests the predicted sharp retention drop between 5/1 and 2/1. The latest m129 sulfur-containing aldehyde labels exposed large acquisition-time overprediction at those ratios, making carbonyl-environment-dependent transfer a useful question.

Measure m129 in neat EA at 100 uL; predicted 5.51/12.67 mL. The matched 1/1 and 2/1 observations b0571346163b8f77528d and e05652bb38d9efd5b11e measured 5.87/10.46 and 6.00/12.38, while cf8ab33c25ad391a584c measured 6.10/17.18 at 5/1. Measure ortho-methoxyacetophenone m127 at 10/1 and 50 uL; predicted 7.49/21.35 mL. The latest same-amount 5/1 result c40d715383d042030e93 measured 6.36/15.33, and the 10/1, 100-uL record aff2ffd59a0610a54995 measured 5.47/21.33. Measure tert-butyl acetoacetate m25 at 5/1 and 50 uL; predicted 10.03/21.82 mL. The matched 10/1 observation 61e2b18d9ec61505948c measured 14.73/24.55 and the neat-EA observation 9fa9fb28b91ddf9af555 measured 4.28/7.28. This fills a missing solvent bridge in a beta-keto ester with a bulky ester group, helping distinguish its onset and completion curvature from other beta-dicarbonyl rows. Its high CW distance supports coverage value, rather than establishing an error.

Measure nitrophenethyl alcohol m200 in neat EA at 50 uL; predicted 7.07/17.27 mL. At 2/1, a92f7617b135de150588 and f91285c618eacb53538b measured 33.88/74.44 and 19.65/68.02 at 50 and 150 uL. Pair with the selected neat-EA high-amount point to test whether this large onset response attenuates at the stronger-solvent boundary. Nitro and hydroxyl interactions offer a transfer test beyond the simpler alcohol family.

Measure the matched m200 neat-EA, 150-uL experiment; predicted 7.05/17.29 mL. The model nearly equates the selected amount endpoints. The measured 1/1 pair 97318de99bab4460cf4e and 5da8c25a3982216fb112 showed a smaller onset decrease than the 2/1 pair, with completion nearly unchanged. This pair tests further attenuation or persistence using recorded conditions alone, and provides a strong-solvent boundary for both endpoints.

Measure 2,6-lutidine m141 in neat EA at 50 uL; predicted 5.49/16.26 mL. The same amount and DCM-loading protocol measured 12.49/23.49 at 1/1 in 835b5f2641442576de42 and 15.70/29.42 at 2/1 in 82d7243f61695e1b94cf. This uncovered boundary tests solvent-response curvature for a sterically substituted basic heteroaromatic, a family with substantial historical errors at weaker ratios. The high CW distance and quantile spans are supporting diagnostics, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

Measure para-cyanoacetophenone m31 at 5/1 and 50 uL; predicted 9.45/30.88 mL. The matched 10/1 record b3d9bb5afa82b99f2a11 measured 31.50/67.28, while the 5/1, 150-uL record eb383b92fe958c91d272 measured 10.39/34.22. This tests a steep solvent transition at fixed low amount and a within-ratio amount contrast in a neutral nitrile-carbonyl environment. Its broad V1 quantile span reinforces the value of resolving this missing anchor.

hypotheses.content: Loading responses depend on molecule, mobile-phase strength and endpoint. The latest m51 10/1 result and m60 5/1 result strengthen substantial onset decreases with amount, while completion changes much less. The completed m45 20/1 series shows continued decreases with diminishing increments. These observations do not establish a universal loading slope or linear interpolation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many candidate predictions barely respond to amount. Matched contrasts can teach substantial endpoint-specific effects and the solvent regions where small responses are appropriate, reducing averaging across environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m51's 10/1 midpoint follow linear onset interpolation, and do m60 and m200 show attenuated loading responses in stronger mobile phase?

hypotheses.content: m125 retains protocol-associated differences in neat EA as well as at 1/1. The latest neat-EA 50-uL pair measured a 7.57-mL completion difference and a 4.23-mL onset difference between the 300- and 500-uL DCM protocols. Earlier 100-uL neat-EA observations had the same direction. Loading-solvent volume alone is not established as the cause.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Nearly identical acquisition predictions again averaged distinct protocol-associated outcomes. Extending the 300-uL protocol's amount curve tests whether an amount-independent early-completion correction is appropriate and supplies additional supervision for recorded protocol features.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 150 uL sample in neat EA, does the 300-uL DCM protocol remain near its measured 50- and 100-uL completions, or develop a later completion?

hypotheses.content: Records with identical recorded conditions can differ substantially, although this variability is not universal. Consequently, m92's single high-amount 5/1 completion should be checked before interpreting the latest three-point series as a reproducible loading-induced upturn.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A targeted same-tuple acquisition can distinguish a useful nonlinear amount relationship from variability arising from information absent from the catalog. It limits repeated attempts to fit isolated exceptional labels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does another m92 5/1, 150-uL EA-loading record reproduce completion near 27.72 mL or fall closer to the recent 19.96-21.06 mL lower-amount results?

hypotheses.content: Late onset remains associated with m73's measured 1/1 region, but the earlier expectation of a reproducible short, ordered interval is weakened. The latest same-tuple record starts 6.29 mL later than the previous 50-uL record and has V2 about 0.09 mL below V1. This limits interpretation of interval shape while leaving the scope of the late-onset association worth testing.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs the scope of an observed solvent-response exception without transferring anomalous endpoint order or a stable narrow interval to neighboring ester conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 2/1 and 50 uL, does m73 retain early onset as at the measured 100-uL boundary, or does late onset extend into this condition?

hypotheses.content: The m128 and m129 sulfur-containing aryl carbonyls may require different strong-solvent transition shapes. Measured m129 onset stays near 6 mL from 5/1 through 1/1, whereas m128 has onset near 19-21 mL at 5/1 and near 7.57 mL at 1/1. The predicted m128 drop by 2/1 and the predicted m129 completion increase in neat EA remain untested. Cross-molecule differences are not isolated causal effects because recorded density and amounts differ.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest m129 labels reject its earlier late-retention predictions in stronger mobile phases. Neighboring measured structures can teach where that correction transfers and where carbonyl environment requires a different curve.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m128's low-amount retention drop sharply by 2/1, and does m129 completion decrease or increase between 1/1 and neat EA?

hypotheses.content: m173's protocol-associated completion difference persists in neat EA, but is condition dependent. The latest 2000-uL DCM protocol finished at 50.30 mL versus 31.91 for the 1500-uL protocol. At 2/1 the protocols finished close together, whereas at 1/1 both were later and differed more substantially. These observations do not identify a mechanism or establish reproducibility.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest result weakens convergence of the protocols in neat EA and argues against a constant protocol offset or a simple monotone completion curve. Retaining this scope prevents incorrect transfer to other acid conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: When an eligible same-tuple record becomes available, does the prolonged neat-EA completion under the 2000-uL protocol recur?

feedback_interpretation: The latest m125 neat-EA pair again produced opposite signed completion errors from nearly equal acquisition predictions: 12.85 versus 20.42 mL. This strengthens a recurring protocol association at two neat-EA amounts and motivates completing the 300-uL protocol's curve, without claiming causality or an unmeasured 150-uL protocol gap. The m51 10/1 low-amount result measured onset 37.67 mL versus 26.24 at 150 uL, while completion differed by only 2.26 mL. The m60 5/1 low-amount onset of 27.63 versus 19.65 at 100 uL supports a related endpoint-specific loading response. I now test midpoint curvature and stronger-solvent attenuation rather than simply adding further weak-solvent endpoints. The m45 20/1 high-amount result continued the onset decrease, from 39.58 to 26.49 to 20.75 mL across 50, 100 and 150 uL, with smaller completion changes; it still does not validate its anomalous 50/1 record. The new m92 5/1 labels finished at 21.06 and 19.96 mL, below the existing 150-uL completion of 27.72. That suggests an upturn but does not establish its reproducibility, so I prioritize another high-amount catalog record. For m73, late onset recurred at 1/1, but the same-tuple discrepancy and slight endpoint reversal weaken a stable narrow-interval interpretation. I move to a neighboring-ratio boundary. The m173 neat-EA completion of 50.30 mL was underestimated by 18.60 mL and retained a substantial protocol difference; its convergence question is now weakened, while reproducibility remains open. The m129 5/1 and 2/1 outcomes were substantially earlier than their acquisition predictions, motivating a related ketone transition and a neat-EA boundary. The m127 5/1 result weakened the previous predicted local response shape and motivates a matched low-amount 10/1 anchor. The m198, m88 and m209 bridge labels were comparatively close to prediction, reducing immediate follow-up priority. Several pending-CW neutral strong-solvent labels also finished earlier than predicted, so I avoid spending the supplements mainly on more of that already-covered region. All errors cited here are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The pending 16 already cover neutral aromatic conditions, several ketone and beta-dicarbonyl points, a tertiary-alcohol neat-EA anchor and a salicylate condition. The supplements add comparisons those labels cannot isolate. The m51 midpoint and three m60 experiments form a local study of hydroxyl-environment, amount and solvent-strength interactions; the m200 neat-EA pair tests whether analogous attenuation extends to a nitro-substituted primary alcohol. These matched comparisons can teach both large onset responses and appropriately small responses, separately from completion. The m92 same-tuple acquisition addresses whether a proposed nonlinear completion response is learnable, while the m125 extension addresses persistent prediction averaging across protocols. The m45 and m73 boundaries constrain the scope of anomalous response shapes rather than repeatedly chasing their problematic intervals. The m128/m129 comparison tests transfer of the latest sulfur-carbonyl correction, and m127, m25, m141 and m31 fill chemically meaningful missing solvent anchors across aromatic ketone, beta-keto ester, basic heteroaromatic and neutral nitrile-carbonyl environments. Repeated molecules serve explicit discriminating comparisons; exploration occurs through uncovered condition relationships within the supplied Row-distribution. Catalog repeats are not assumed to be controlled technical replicates. Quantile spans and CW percentiles provide diagnostic context, and neither is treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. Elution interval width remains an outcome. The 16 selected IDs, together with the pending 16 and their supplied premeasurement predictions, fix the full batch before any new label reveal; predictions shown in reasons are rounded only for readability.
